title: A Window That Follows the Cells

scenes.tts: Why can a few days with one eye closed reshape a young mouse's cortex, but change an adult's much less?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Window That Follows the Cells. A young mouse and an adult mouse side by side, each with one eye closed.
scenes.narration: Why can a few days with one eye closed reshape a young mouse's cortex, but change an adult's much less?

scenes.tts: In the binocular zone of mouse visual cortex, most neurons answer both eyes, and some answer only one.
scenes.visual: Mouse head from above; the binocular zone of primary visual cortex lights up. One example cortical cell with two input lines, one from each eye.
scenes.narration: In the binocular zone of mouse visual cortex, most neurons answer both eyes, and some answer only one.

scenes.tts: Most cells answer the eye on the opposite side of the head more strongly.
scenes.visual: The contralateral input line is drawn thick, the ipsilateral line thin. Labels: contralateral (opposite side), ipsilateral (same side).
scenes.narration: Most cells answer the eye on the opposite side of the head more strongly.

scenes.tts: The ocular dominance index puts a number on that preference. This example cell scores zero point five.
scenes.caption: The ocular dominance index puts a number on that preference. This example cell scores 0.50.
scenes.visual: On screen: index = (C − I)/(C + I). Example cell: C = 30, I = 10 spikes per second, index 0.50. A bar sits at +0.5 on a scale from −1 to +1.
scenes.narration: The ocular dominance index puts a number on that preference. This example cell scores 0.50.

scenes.tts: Now close the opposite eye for about four days, at postnatal day twenty-eight.
scenes.caption: Now close the opposite eye for about four days, at postnatal day 28.
scenes.visual: A lid closes over the contralateral eye. A four-day clock spins. Label: P28.
scenes.narration: Now close the opposite eye for about four days, at postnatal day 28.

scenes.tts: Responses shift toward the open eye. This example cell's score falls below zero.
scenes.visual: The bar swings from +0.5 to below zero. Label: illustrative cell, C = 12, I = 18 spikes per second, index −0.20. The contralateral line thins; the ipsilateral line now dominates.
scenes.narration: Responses shift toward the open eye. This example cell's score falls below zero.

scenes.tts: In young mice, most of that shift comes from the closed eye's responses weakening.
scenes.visual: The closed eye's input line thins a lot; the open eye's line thickens only slightly (in the example, C 30 to 12, I 10 to 18).
scenes.narration: In young mice, most of that shift comes from the closed eye's responses weakening.

scenes.tts: Pause and predict. Do the same thing to a two-month-old mouse. What happens to the score?
scenes.visual: Predict card: same four days, one eye closed, at two months old (P60). Shift or not?
scenes.narration: Pause and predict. Do the same thing to a two-month-old mouse. What happens to the score?

scenes.tts: Much less. In mice the shift is largest near postnatal day twenty-eight.
scenes.caption: Much less. In mice the shift is largest near postnatal day 28.
scenes.visual: The bar moves much less. A timeline from P0 to P60 appears with a peak at P28.
scenes.narration: Much less. In mice the shift is largest near postnatal day 28.

scenes.tts: It is much smaller before about day nineteen, or after about day thirty-two.
scenes.caption: It is much smaller before about day 19, or after about day 32.
scenes.visual: A sand-coloured band from P19 to P32 on the timeline. Credit: Gordon and Stryker, 1996.
scenes.narration: It is much smaller before about day 19, or after about day 32.

scenes.tts: So the window lies in a few weeks of youth. Is that age itself, or something age brings?
scenes.visual: The band on the timeline, with two labels hovering over it: age? or something age brings?
scenes.narration: So the window lies in a few weeks of youth. Is that age itself, or something age brings?

scenes.tts: Here is the idea to carry through. The window follows the inhibitory cells, not the calendar.
scenes.visual: Card: The window follows the inhibitory cells, not the calendar.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea to carry through. The window follows the inhibitory cells, not the calendar.

scenes.tts: A working model: maturing inhibition, especially from parvalbumin basket cells, opens the window once it passes a threshold.
scenes.visual: Label: working model. Inhibition, drawn as a parvalbumin basket cell, grows bolder along the timeline. A dashed threshold line; the band begins where it crosses.
scenes.narration: A working model: maturing inhibition, especially from parvalbumin basket cells, opens the window once it passes a threshold.

scenes.tts: As inhibition keeps maturing, and brakes build up around these cells, it closes.
scenes.visual: Brakes gather around the basket cell; the band ends.
scenes.narration: As inhibition keeps maturing, and brakes build up around these cells, it closes.

scenes.tts: In young cortex, a brief boost of inhibition was enough to start a window. The boost did not have to last.
scenes.visual: Label: young cortex. A switch flips once at the threshold and a band begins; a second label on the band: later closed by further maturation and brakes. No countdown clock.
scenes.narration: In young cortex, a brief boost of inhibition was enough to start a window. The boost did not have to last.

scenes.tts: The rule covers this young shift in mouse and rat visual cortex. Adults keep a weaker, different form. It does not cover people, or song and language.
scenes.visual: Scope card: mouse and rat primary visual cortex, juvenile shift. Adults: weaker, different form. Outside: people; song and language windows.
scenes.narration: The rule covers this young shift in mouse and rat visual cortex. Adults keep a weaker, different form. It does not cover people, or song and language.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: the window is set by the state of a circuit, not simply by age.
scenes.visual: Closing card: set by the state of a circuit, not simply by age.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: the window is set by the state of a circuit, not simply by age.
